expectations.text: Uses the CMMC scoping categories: CUI assets, Security Protection Assets, Contractor Risk Managed Assets, Specialized Assets, and out-of-scope assets — with the required treatment of each
expectations.evidence: CUI Assets — fully assessed against all 110... Security Protection Assets... assessed for the security capability... CRMA... assessed at reduced depth... Specialized Assets... documented with compensating controls... Out-of-Scope Assets... excluded entirely, but you must document the rationale

expectations.text: Endorses the enclave strategy: concentrate CUI processing/storage/transmission into a bounded environment to shrink the assessment boundary
expectations.evidence: An enclave approach is the right instinct... it shrinks the assessment boundary, reduces the number of in-scope assets

expectations.text: Requires dataflow mapping: where CUI enters, moves, is stored, and exits (email, file shares, endpoints, cloud)
expectations.evidence: Trace where CUI enters your environment (email, portal, physical media...), where it's processed... where it's stored (file shares, databases, backups), and where it exits

expectations.text: Covers external service providers: CSPs handling CUI need FedRAMP Moderate (or equivalency); ESPs/MSPs are in scope via Security Protection Asset treatment
expectations.evidence: Covers CSPs ('must be FedRAMP Authorized at Moderate or equivalent — this is a DFARS 7012 requirement') but never addresses ESPs/MSPs being in scope via Security Protection Asset treatment

expectations.text: Covers flow-down: subcontractors receiving CUI need Level 2; FCI-only subs need Level 1 — with the DFARS 7012 clause flowing down
expectations.evidence: Mentions 'subcontractor flow-down' only as a CUI exit path; never states Level 2 for CUI subs, Level 1 for FCI-only subs, or DFARS 7012 clause flow-down
